# Studio workbench

The local product panel is served at /studio. Open the launcher's /studio#CONTROL_TOKEN link. The browser removes the fragment and retains only the human control token in the existing tab-scoped arcane-lab-session storage entry. Each browser request uses the local bearer, omits cookies, refuses redirects, and supplies Origin automatically on POST. Native fetch is called as a plain function so it does not receive StudioApi as its receiver.

## Studio API keys and operations

The default connection card issues an Arcane API key through POST /v1/studio/keys with explicit allowedRoots and allowWrites. Workspace is selected and writes are disabled by default. The returned key must match arcane_local_v1_PORT_64HEX, this exact literal loopback daemon port, and the human-selected service grants. The plugin infers its local endpoint from the key: open Arcane in Studio’s Plugins toolbar, paste the key, and press Connect. The workbench has no plugin daemon URL or pairing-code inputs or instructions.

The raw API key is returned only on issuance. It starts masked; Reveal key and Copy API key are separate explicit actions. Dismiss secret, in-page navigation, session selection, link navigation and page exit clear the secret from memory and DOM. A response arriving after navigation cannot redisplay it. Browser history restoration resumes refresh with the secret cleared. No API key is added to browser storage. Copying writes to the clipboard only after the user clicks Copy API key.

GET /v1/studio/keys renders metadata only: key ID, roots, write permission, issue/revocation dates and reported last use. The UI refuses a list containing raw keys. API key access & revocation provides a human confirmation for POST /v1/studio/keys/revoke {keyId}; the confirmation displays metadata only. A lost issuance or revocation response is not replayed automatically. The UI refreshes recorded key metadata, then requires an explicit human acknowledgement before another mutation; raw secrets cannot be recovered from history.

Keys are persisted as hashes by the parent-owned store and remain revocable. Human control credentials protect listing, issuance and revocation; scoped native agent credentials cannot grant plugin access. A connected window is chosen by its exact session ID and clientSessionId; place ID and display path never substitute for window or instance identity. Legacy one-use pairing endpoints remain compatible at the lower protocol layer and are absent from the default view.

Browse, search, selection, inspect and source reads use /v1/studio/commands. Returned opaque refs can be selected or copied. Property and editor baselines are captured only from succeeded read receipts whose result ref matches the original request and exact client session. Expected fields come from those receipts. Editable properties, creation classes and source sizes remain bounded by the bridge contract.

History displays queued, dispatched, succeeded, failed, cancelled and needs_reconciliation distinctly. The workbench requires fresh exact-session history and heartbeat before sending commands. An unknown POST retains its original UUID and payload; only an explicit identical command retry reuses the idempotency key. Restore sends only commandId and a fresh requestId to /v1/studio/restore. Its confirmation shows before, after and exact session; the plugin compares current after-state before restoring.

## Durable work and human review

The Work queue reads GET /v1/work/runs and GET /v1/work/ready independently of Studio availability. It shows durable run IDs, task keys, file scopes, dependencies, worker labels, lease expiry, progress, review notes and recorded evidence. Ready status comes from the ready endpoint; completion is never inferred from a worker summary. The authored Project build board remains a separate view of /v1/product/state.

Create a scoped work run expands a structured editor for 1–64 tasks. Each task has a unique key, instructions, acceptance criteria, explicit relative file scopes and a dependency list. The UI checks missing keys, cycles and unsafe scope syntax; the WorkStore remains authoritative for filesystem links, leases and file hashes. POST /v1/work/create records the graph. It does not launch a worker or claim file access.

Select a submitted task to read its evidence paths, SHA-256 digests, byte counts, notes and submission times. A nonempty human decision note and an explicit confirmation are required before POST /v1/work/review. Approve verifies unchanged evidence through the daemon and releases dependent tasks; Request changes returns the task to pending. The confirmation is rejected locally if the displayed submission changed while it was open. Review requires the human control token and exact browser Origin; scoped agent tokens cannot review. The UI does not expose worker lease tokens or silently claim, submit or approve tasks.

Create and review have no idempotency key. An ambiguous response blocks further work decisions, refreshes only through GET, and requires the human to inspect recorded runs and explicitly acknowledge that inspection before a new decision. These pending ambiguity notices are in-memory UI state; recorded runs and decisions survive browser reloads and daemon restarts in WorkStore.

## Native Studio read diagnostics

Native Studio diagnostics uses the existing human-only GET /v1/native/capabilities and POST /v1/native/read routes. Opening the panel sends neither request. Observe tools & Studio windows enumerates capabilities and exact native IDs without a targeted read. The picker starts empty, including when only one window is present. The human must select an observed studio_id and send each read explicitly. Native IDs are independent of Arcane plugin session IDs, place IDs and names.

The UI offers only the adapter's seven read methods. Runtime tools must also be allowed and report read-only, non-destructive annotations; unsupported selection, evaluation, writes and play controls remain unavailable. Tree requests require a datamodel and enforce limits of 1–200 results and depth 1–10. Instance/script paths are bounded to 1024 characters, queries to 256, and optional classes to 100. Script reads always request an explicit ordered inclusive range of at most 500 lines, with line numbers from 1 through 1,000,000. Unused fields are disabled and omitted. The adapter re-enumerates Studio windows before forwarding the exact requested ID. An absent target disables reading and requires a new observation and explicit selection; another window is never substituted.

Only a receipt matching the exact request's studio_id and method can supply output, including HTTP tool-error receipts. Metadata must report connected:false, consistent provenance/transport, and bounded request usage. A successful response or matching tool error can report that its connection closed after that request. Errors without a valid receipt, including cleanup failure, explicitly say closure was not reported. Connection counters in the fixture controller verify cleanup independently of these UI labels.

Request and target epochs discard late successes and errors after target changes, including switching away and back to the original ID. Page exit clears native inventory, selection and receipt state; restored pages require another explicit observation. An earlier lifecycle's response or finally handler cannot overwrite a newer request's output or busy state. Capability observations, target changes and new reads clear previous output/provenance together. The metadata view identifies inventory versus read, exact target, method, evidence kind, observation time and request limits; it does not present a persistent connection.

Output, inventory names, server metadata and error messages use text DOM APIs. Local control/scoped/key secrets and common credential fields are redacted; ANSI/control characters are removed. The UI bounds HTTP response bytes to 512 KiB and cancels oversized streams. Display text is capped at 64 KiB plus a visible truncation notice, preserving UTF-8 character boundaries. The adapter additionally enforces a 100 KiB source response limit. The result is keyboard-focusable, and the request status is announced through a polite live region.

## Native Codex conversation

Conversation uses human-only GET /v1/codex/state and POST /v1/codex/action. Mounting, opening the panel, typing, polling and restoring the page read metadata only. They never connect a CLI, select a model, create/resume a thread, start a turn, grant writes or answer native approvals. Each mutation requires the corresponding explicit human control. The existing launcher token stays in the shared tab-scoped entry; Codex adds no browser storage. Agent tokens cannot access either route.

Connect reads account and model metadata from the native service. Model and effort pickers both start empty and use only the reported catalogue; an exact pair must be explicitly acknowledged before Start read-only thread or Resume exact thread can run. There is no default effort, alias substitution, fallback model or entitlement claim. Resume sends the pasted exact native thread ID. Every subsequent action carries the reported connection ID and relevant thread, turn and approval handle. Native tool profile metadata always reports verified:false; Studio access remains separate.

Submit starts one native turn with bounded nonempty public text, at most 128 KiB in UTF-8. Native acknowledgement and native turn completion are displayed separately. The transcript uses monotonic event seq values to deduplicate overlapping snapshots, preserving identical consecutive chunks. Messages are grouped by exact thread/turn/item identity even when items interleave. It reports missing sequences, native dropped events and display truncation. Only public deltas render as text. Reasoning/item payloads, HTML and native image payloads do not render. Native image and design verification remain open.

Threads start read-only. Grant workspace writes shows the exact connection, thread, turn and workspace in a checkbox confirmation. Approval acceptance shows every scope ID plus the full bounded command/cwd or file diffs, requires the current native eligibility and exact thread grant, and re-reads current state before sending. A changed preview, scope, grant or expiry invalidates confirmation. Decline, cancel, interrupt, revoke and disconnect remain available as safety actions during pending or uncertain work. Revoking writes during an active turn closes the connection; it does not undo edits. Safety actions fence delayed earlier replies, including replies with no newer event sequence.

HTTP failures and unreadable/mismatched receipts retain the original request UUID and block normal mutations. No POST is automatically retried. Read recorded actions & state performs GET only. An explicit acknowledgement can clear the browser block after an acknowledged/rejected receipt or a settled change of connection scope; a native unknown receipt on the same connection stays blocked. Disconnect followed by inspection and a new explicit connect cannot revive the old grant or replay the old turn. Reload recovers applicable pending/unknown IDs from the durable service journal. Page exit aborts metadata reads, clears displayed conversation text and confirmation, and fences late responses; restoration only refreshes recorded state.

All server text uses text DOM APIs with control/ANSI removal and credential redaction. HTTP JSON is bounded to 4 MiB and must be valid UTF-8. Each public message is capped at 64 KiB, with at most 128 messages and 512 KiB of display text. Approval previews are complete within their accepted bounds; an invalid or oversized snapshot disables normal actions instead of presenting an inferred approval.

## Native agent connection

Get scoped agent token explicitly POSTs {} to /v1/product/mcp-token with the human browser credential. It accepts only a distinct token with canReview:false and expires:daemon lifetime. The returned scopes and token are displayed in the panel; Copy scoped agent token requires a separate click. The agent token is kept only in memory and the ephemeral DOM, cleared on page exit and replaced only by an explicit handoff. It is never added to localStorage or sessionStorage.

The PowerShell setup displayed in the panel uses ARCANE_DAEMON_URL for this daemon origin, ARCANE_LOCAL_TOKEN for the scoped agent token, and npm run launch:native. The human control token is not inserted into these terminal instructions. A daemon restart requires a fresh launch link and scoped token. This scoped native agent token is separate from the Studio plugin API key and cannot issue, list or revoke Studio keys. Provider credentials are not used by this flow.

## Asset workshop

The panel uses the parent's fixed-template API:

- POST /v1/assets/probe with {} for observed installed runtime capabilities.
- GET /v1/assets/jobs for recorded job identity, state, stages and errors.
- POST /v1/assets/start with bounded AssetInput fields only.
- POST /v1/assets/cancel with the exact selected jobId.
- GET /v1/assets/manifest?jobId=... for a verified completed manifest.
- GET /v1/assets/preview?jobId=...&path=... for authenticated PNG bytes.

Only hero-prop and environment-kit are offered. Size defaults follow the selected template. Slugs, meters, colors, seed, triangle budget, render resolution and samples use the pipeline's bounds. Start requires a successful runtime probe, no running job and no interrupted supervision. Missing endpoints visibly disable actions; no runtime, stages or completion states are fabricated. A job start or cancellation with an unknown outcome is never replayed automatically.

Manifest loading checks the selected job and request identity, then fetches only preview-hero.png and preview-side.png with the bearer header. The browser compares preview bytes and SHA-256 against the manifest and decodes them into canvas elements. It puts no token in preview URLs and creates no blob image URL, so previews work under the parent's self-only image CSP. The panel displays the mesh audit, artifact hashes, warnings and limitations. Export/import quality and Roblox scale remain separate review requirements.

## Verification

Use npm run typecheck for the root no-emit check. For isolated UI verification, compile tests/unit/studio-ui.test.ts with the repository compiler and strict NodeNext settings into a temporary output directory. ARCANE_UI_BUILD_DIR selects the emitted browser JS for the HTTP fixture. When ARCANE_UI_BUILD_DIR is set, the real-daemon browser test also serves that emitted browser source through its Playwright response fixture. No root dist artifact needs to be overwritten.

Set ARCANE_UI_BROWSER_MODULE to an existing Playwright index.mjs and ARCANE_UI_BROWSER_EXE to an installed Chromium browser. Run node --test against the emitted studio-ui.test.js. ARCANE_UI_SCREENSHOT optionally saves desktop/mobile screenshots and focused panel captures; supply a path ending in .png. Temporary output can reference the repository’s existing node_modules through a temporary junction when parent-owned daemon routes import dependencies. No root dependencies are installed by this workflow.

As verified on 2026-10-11, all 24 focused checks passed with Microsoft Edge, including API-key grant/format/port validation, metadata-only history, masked/revealed/copied secrets, dismissal/navigation cleanup, revocation and lost-response handling, the native-fetch receiver regression, safe DOM/CSP, exact references and baselines, restore and ambiguity recovery, responsive layout, fixed-template asset control and authenticated preview corruption rejection. The asset/command browser server is explicitly an HTTP contract fixture: its synthetic runtime and preview bytes are not native integration evidence. A second browser test runs real daemon routes with temporary SQLite WorkStore state and real evidence files: human key issuance and scoped-agent denial, key-based HTTP plugin connection, reported last use, revocation of the key and its connected session, persistent key metadata without raw secrets, create, scoped-token handoff, human Origin enforcement, hash conflict, changes requested, re-submission, approval, readiness, lost create response, reload and daemon restart all passed.

All 16 existing native HTTP controller fixture checks and the root no-emit typecheck also passed. The native diagnostics browser test mounts the actual nativeRoutes and NativeStudioSession with an injected in-memory SDK server; it records 37 fresh fixture connections opened and 37 closed, with 19 explicitly targeted fixture reads. It verifies multiple and single-window non-selection, stale-ID refusal, agent denial, allowlist/bounds, safe text and redaction, exact success/error receipts, failed-cleanup reporting, target round trips, page lifecycle events, and an old response arriving during a newer request. These are API/controller and browser fixtures, not native plugin or live Studio proof.

The key-based plugin exchange in these tests is an explicitly labeled HTTP protocol client. No actual native Studio plugin operation, Blender generation, Roblox asset import or Hunted place change was performed by this UI work. Live native Studio testing, including native UI and reads, remains explicitly deferred until a later user request.

## Native Codex conversation panel

The Conversation panel shares the existing human-only tab token. Mounting, expanding or refreshing it reads bounded state; it never connects a native client, selects a model, creates/resumes a thread, grants writes, or submits a turn automatically. Native execution is an explicit human action. Model and effort must match the reported catalogue exactly; catalogue presence does not prove entitlement. Read-only threads are the default. Workspace grants and exact-scoped command/file approval decisions are separate, deliberate confirmations with complete bounded plain-text previews.

POST /v1/codex/action carries a UUID request ID plus the exact connection/thread/turn/approval scope. An unknown HTTP/native outcome blocks ordinary new work until inspected. The browser reads durable action receipts to reconcile a lost response; it does not replay the prompt. Interrupt, revoke and disconnect remain independent of a pending ordinary request. Reconnection cannot revive old grants or accept old approvals. The host refuses agent lifecycle/approval access and browser executable/config/env fields.

Public deltas deduplicate by (connection ID, sequence), not text: identical consecutive chunks survive, interleaved items keep their thread/turn/item identity, and missing/evicted sequence ranges are shown. Private reasoning is not rendered. Content, filenames, commands and diffs are untrusted text. The stream is bounded and is not a durable complete transcript; native conversation history remains owned by the CLI. The Arcane MCP profile is labelled requested/configured, verified:false until actual native tool acceptance. Image/design/native media feature acceptance remains open.

Current fixture evidence: runtime/verification/codex-ui/codex-chat-test.log reports 11/11 passing, zero skipped, including installed Edge 155.0.4283.45 with the actual human-only service and both synthetic-host and spawned-Node JSONL peers. runtime/verification/codex-ui/studio-shell-test.log reports all 33 existing workbench checks passing, zero skipped. Desktop/mobile captures and approval/conversation/unknown-outcome captures are under the same directory. Parent inspected the responsive desktop/mobile panel captures. These are real browser/protocol/controller fixtures, not installed Codex model inference or live Studio proof. Subsequent client security changes require renewed integration regression.


## Reference-led workspace update (2026-10-12)

The initial view now follows the supplied Arcane reference: a charcoal/red branded rail and navigation, tool tabs, central conversation and anchored model/composer controls, and a right-hand artifact preview. Advanced session/key/command/receipt/work controls remain available below the workspace through navigation. Every one of the original 241 control IDs is retained. The house in the reference is not a hardcoded model or demo success: only selected, authenticated, manifest-verified Blender previews populate the artifact pane. Export files are tied to the exact completed job and independently checked by SHA-256 before an explicit browser download.

Workspace navigation, search, keyboard shortcuts, draft cards, collapse and fullscreen are DOM-only. Drafts never submit, create native threads, connect providers or grant permissions. Navigation clears issuance secrets. The asset download client cancels/discards stale selections and page-exit results. The provider lab shares the same restrained palette and accessible empty states without fabricated accounts, entitlements, quotas or billing.

Current focused acceptance: 50/50 checks passed from fresh compiled source, including real Edge native-conversation and Studio HTTP/service fixtures and five artifact-download client checks; no skipped browser checks. This is not native Studio or additional real model inference proof. The earlier current-source root run was 359/360 with a missing asset-download module in one fixture map; that route was corrected and the focused rerun passed. The full final root rerun is recorded separately.

### OneDrive compiler input repair

The native TypeScript glob skipped genuine Windows cloud-placeholder files, leaving old Studio UI code even after a nominally successful build. The build wrapper now enumerates bounded real source files with Node lstat/realpath, excludes hidden generated metadata, and passes an explicit files configuration to the fixed pinned compiler. Temporary configuration stays in ignored runtime/build and is removed only as the exact owned single file. This repairs the underlying compilation rather than suppressing UI errors. Source-map provenance is checked when packaging. Per-child memory limits, host overrides and invalid-flag refusal remain verified.

### Brand asset

apps/desktop/public/brand/arcane-ridges.png is original raster branding generated with the built-in image tool: dark basalt mountain ridges, restrained ember-red fissures, charcoal fog, generous dark space, no text/logo/UI. The Arcane mark itself is deterministic inline SVG. No illustrative house image is included in the application or package.
